record.question:
A clinic runs Windows applications on EC2. Security policy requires scheduled installation of approved operating-system patches and notification whenever a running instance uses an AMI outside an approved list. Developers must still be able to launch an unapproved AMI for investigation. All instances meet Systems Manager managed-node prerequisites.

Which actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Attach an IAM policy that denies RunInstances when the requested AMI is not on the approved list.
Enable GuardDuty and use its threat findings as the authoritative record of missing operating-system patches and unapproved AMIs.
Schedule AWS-RunPatchBaseline with Scan for all Windows instances. Treat a successful scan and its compliance report as evidence that all approved updates have been installed.
Define approved patches in a Systems Manager Patch Manager baseline and schedule AWS-RunPatchBaseline with Install, an appropriate reboot policy, and compliance reporting.
Record EC2 instances in AWS Config and configure the approved-amis-by-id managed rule. Route NON_COMPLIANT compliance-change events through EventBridge to an SNS topic.

explanation.text:
Correct: <<4>> and <<5>>. Patch Manager defines and installs approved updates on managed nodes. AWS Config evaluates running instances against the AMI list, and EventBridge routes compliance changes to the notification target. This is a detective control, so it does not prevent a launch.

<<1>> is a preventive control and conflicts with the requirement to permit investigation instances.

<<2>> is incorrect because GuardDuty threat detection does not replace the patch installation workflow or the specified AMI allow-list evaluation.

<<3>> checks patch compliance but does not install updates. A successful Scan execution does not establish that the machine is patched; installation and any required reboot remain separate actions.

<<4>> requires an execution schedule as well as a baseline: approval rules alone do not install patches. <<5>> requires Config resource recording and permissions for the EventBridge-to-SNS delivery. Distinguish patch compliance, image compliance, and threat detection when selecting controls.

Official AWS references (checked 2026-09-18):
[AWS-RunPatchBaseline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager-aws-runpatchbaseline.html)
[Approved AMI rule](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/approved-amis-by-id.html)
[Config events in EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/monitor-config-with-cloudwatchevents.html)

diagram_alt: Patch installation and AMI detection are independent controls; notification follows a permitted launch.

sources.supports: Detects running instances using AMIs outside the configured list
Compliance-change events can invoke notification targets

editorial_notes: Preserved two-answer key and detective-control requirement; completed the baseline option with installation and scheduling rather than implying baseline creation patches instances.
Root review replaced unrelated Shield patching distractor with the supported Scan versus Install distinction.
